method.test: circular-shift permutation on the condition mask (preserves both the autocorrelation of returns and the block shape of astro windows)
method.resamples: 2000 to screen; anything at p<=0.01 re-tested with 200000. Reason: a permutation p cannot go below 1/(N+1), so a 2000-shift test could never reach the Bonferroni bar and 'no survivors' would have been guaranteed by the method rather than discovered in the data.
method.known_conservatism: Astro conditions recur on their own periods (Mercury goes retrograde about every 116 days). When the mask is rotated by roughly a whole period it lands back on itself, reproducing the original effect and counting as a 'hit' against us. That makes this test CONSERVATIVE for periodic conditions — verified on synthetic data, where a deliberately planted +0.40%/day effect scored p=7.6e-4 rather than the 2e-5 floor. The bias runs against finding astro effects, which is the correct direction for a claim this desk is trying to kill rather than confirm — but it means a null result here is 'not demonstrated', never 'disproved'. Read the effect sizes, not only the p-values.
method.tested_on: INDIVIDUAL STOCKS (99 with >=1000 bars), plus KSE100 and KMI30 separately. Sectors are deliberately NOT tested here: averaging a sector's members together dilutes any stock-specific effect toward zero, and sector moves belong to the macro lens (flows, debt, gold, geopolitics), not to astrology.
method.stock_returns: MARKET-ADJUSTED: r_stock - beta*r_KSE100proxy, beta estimated over the full sample and clamped to [0,3]. Raw returns would measure beta, not astrology — a weak market tilt shows up multiplied in every high-beta name and masquerades as a stock-specific discovery. Index tests stay RAW, since a market-wide claim is exactly what they are meant to catch.

KMI30 (proxy).note: weights are KSE100 weights renormalised within the KMI30 set

method.index_caveat: No real daily index history exists in reach (Yahoo's ^KSE is monthly and ends in 2021; DPS publishes indices live-only; stooq has none), so each index is rebuilt from TODAY's constituents cap-weighted by current weight_pct. That carries survivorship bias and weight drift, which shifts the LEVEL of returns — but this test compares returns inside vs outside astro windows, and the bias is present in both, so it does not manufacture or hide an astro effect. Labelled a proxy everywhere it appears.
method.multiple_comparisons: BOTH reported: Bonferroni (family-wise) at p < 1.90e-05 across 2589 hypotheses, AND Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 5% (cutoff p <= 0.00e+00). Bonferroni alone is brutal at this width and could hide a real-but-modest effect; reporting both means the verdict cannot be blamed on the choice of correction.

headline.verdict: No astro condition has a demonstrated edge on PSX. Tested stock by stock (not averaged into sectors, which would have hidden any stock-specific effect) and on KSE100 and KMI30 separately, across ~19 years. Nothing survived the multiplicity correction at all. The desk publishes this rather than hiding it: the astro lens must not be presented as if it had an edge it cannot show.
headline.read_this_before_the_numbers: At p<0.05 you would expect about 129.5 false positives from 2589 tests by luck alone; 143 came back. Raw hits below are published for transparency, not because they are real.

convergence.note: Per STOCK: does the data's best graha match the one tradition assigns to that stock's sector (astro_map.json)? With 9 grahas, blind chance agrees about 11% of the time — so compare the rate below against ~11%, not against zero.
